page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a heading above it and a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: De cuculo.
main_text.p: Avium, quae in humanos usus & cibos ad-mittuntur, agmen claudet cuculus, cuius carnes omnium esse suavissimas, gravissimus Philosophus, locupletissima, velut alterum copiae cornu, veterum autorum bibliotheca, Plinius lib.10 cap.9. prodidit. Nec mirum, quod in alienis pariat nidis, maxime palumbium, alauda & curruca atque etiam lute-la[?]; singula quoque ponat ova, bona rarò quod nulla alia avis; pullus item eius subdatur & educetur, avidumque, is ex natura cibos reliquis pullis praripiat, indeque pinguescat, nitidumque nutricem in se convertat ac devoret, ut nullam ita avium suavitate carnes comparari cum cuculi carne posse verisimile sit quidem, dubium tamen, an nutriendi vi succique probitate cum aliis sit aequiparanda. Ego quod hic statuam, non habeo, nec scio, gula proceribus experimentum relinquo. De pullis cuculi, minus certi aliquid licet affirmare, quos Aristoteles ait, neminem vidisse, nam in lib.6.& 9.histor. cuculum non facere nidum constantem asserit. Et hac de cuculo. Hactenus de alimentis quae veniunt à volucribus, seu volatilibus, sequuntur hu-mi gradientia.

page.notes: The large initial A of "Avium" is a woodcut letter joined to the first word. "lutecula" is at a line end and the reading of its last syllables is doubtful. The running head reads "PROROGANDA." in spaced capitals; it may be "PRÆROGANDA" in the original. The page number is printed in old-style figures at the top right. The closing lines of the paragraph are set indented and centred but continue the same sentence, so they are kept in one paragraph.
